tools.name: verify_output
tools.description: Verify an AI answer against real sources before anyone acts on it. Send a question; Oathlayer answers it, checks the answer against independent sources, and returns the answer, a state, a plain-language message (the tag), a color, and a permanent doc number anyone can verify free at oathlayer.com/ve

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.oathlayer.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_output · Private data: verify_output · Public sink: verify_output.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_output · Private data: verify_output · Public sink: verify_output

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "verify_output" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Submit a question to Oathlayer for verification. Returns whether the answer is approved, unverified, reflects multiple perspectives, is too complex to verify, or needs clarification. Also returns a permanent doc reference number." → after: "Verify an AI answer against real sources before anyone acts on it. Send a question; Oathlayer answers it, checks the answer against independent sources, and returns the answer, a state, a plain-language message (the tag), a color, and a permanent doc number anyone can verify free at oathlayer.com/ve"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
